$comment: Log-based metric definitions for the Cloud Logging project that receives
api-dev and api-prod logs. Each entry is the body of a
logging.projects.metrics.create call and is applied by ./apply.sh.
These exist because the API pushes OpenTelemetry over OTLP and no collector
is deployed: the gauges in backend/src/common/telemetry are real, but until
an OTLP endpoint exists nothing receives them. The structured log line the
same code writes does arrive, so the alertable copy of each signal is
derived from logs. If a collector is ever deployed, these stay valid and the
alerts can be rewritten against the OTLP metrics without changing behavior.
labelExtractors never read a user-supplied field. Every label below is an
enum, a queue name, a deployment environment or a release SHA — see
docs/20-deployment-observability.md section 6 for the rule this follows.

metrics.name: api_process_started
metrics.description: One per API process start. Doubles as the deployment annotation: a new release SHA appearing here is a rollout, and several starts of one SHA in a few minutes is a restart loop.

metrics.name: api_readiness_check_failed
metrics.description: Readiness answered 503 because PostgreSQL did not respond.

metrics.name: api_readiness_latency_ms
metrics.description: How long the readiness database probe took, recorded only when it exceeded the slow threshold. A connection that is merely slow still passes the check, so this is the only signal that shows pool or provider pressure before it becomes an outage.

metrics.name: api_worker_backlog_heartbeat
metrics.description: One per worker backlog report, emitted about once a minute per queue whether the queue is busy or idle. Its absence is the alert: a worker that stopped running fails nothing and logs nothing else.

metrics.name: api_worker_oldest_pending_age_seconds
metrics.description: Age of the oldest item a queue has not finished. Depth alone cannot tell a busy worker from a stopped one; this can.

metrics.name: api_worker_dead_letter_depth
metrics.description: Items a queue exhausted its retries on. These stop aging, so they vanish from the lag signal and need one of their own.

metrics.name: api_database_errors
metrics.description: Errors raised by the Prisma client, by class. Neon's own connection and storage limits are not visible from this project, so this and api_readiness_latency_ms are the whole database signal on our side; the quota half lives in Neon and is alerted there.

metrics.name: api_store_reconciliation_finished
metrics.description: One per completed store reconciliation sweep. The sweep runs from a GitHub Actions cron, so a sweep that stops being scheduled fails nothing at all — its absence is the outage worth catching.
